title: Minimum Window Subsequence
statement:
You are given two strings `a` and `b` of lowercase letters. Find the **shortest substring** of `a` that contains `b` as a **subsequence**.

A substring is a contiguous block of `a`. `b` is a subsequence of that block if you can obtain `b` by deleting zero or more characters from the block without reordering the rest.

If several substrings have the same minimum length, choose the one that starts **leftmost** in `a`. If no substring of `a` contains `b` as a subsequence, the answer is `-1`.

**Follow-up:** the interviewer asked you to explain the DP table behind your solution: what each cell means and how it is filled.
input_format:
The first line contains the string `a`.
The second line contains the string `b`.
output_format: Print the shortest (leftmost on ties) substring of `a` that contains `b` as a subsequence, or `-1` if there is none.
constraints: a and b consist of lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: Both abxc (indices 2 to 5) and abyc (indices 6 to 9) have length 4 and contain a, b, c in order. No shorter window works, and abxc starts further left.
The window aa has no b. The window ab (indices 1 to 2) is the shortest one containing a then b.
All three letters occur but never in the order a, b, c, so no window works.

hints: Let dp[j] be the latest start index of a window ending at the current position in which the first j letters of b appear as a subsequence.

Scan a left to right. When a[i] equals b[j-1], the window for j letters ending at i starts where the window for j-1 letters (ending before i) started. Update j in decreasing order so you read old values.
Whenever dp[|b|] is set, the window is [dp[|b|], i]. Keep the shortest one, and only replace it with a strictly shorter one so ties stay leftmost.
